title: Hire "human" kinda worst advice nowadays.
author: Free-Version-2746
selftext:
For artist don't know anything about code. Say hire programmer. Guess what? 99% that programmer will tell claude code thing for him and take the money as middle man.

Same for programmer. He will likely got scammed by AI artist (price is cheap and yeah, same as artist to code tech guy can't tell different at all)

comments.author: egonosz
comments.body:
I am 100% sure you never worked in game industry. 

Hiring capable programmer or artist who has experience with game development can give you edge. They can follow your vision and make your game better because of domain specific knowledge.

However I would hire only people who are professionals and who I can get recommendations for from other industry professionals.

By the way there is a big difference, how a programmer with game development knowledge prompts Claude and how a designer will prompt it.

comments.author: thecrustycrap
comments.body:
The difference is that they can dive down to the bug that is causing the issue and start working on it. They don’t just throw their hands up in the air and say I don’t know how to fix this once the codebase grows to a point where even Claude code can’t determine which part of the code is causing this. The programmers know where to find the bug, even if they use ai to solve it.

If I’m given a choice between having one or none, I sure as hell want one, so they can maintain the codebase, but paying them for such a high salary for my low chance of success indie game? I’d rather spend it on marketing, or ai tools honestly

comments.author: unfamily_friendly
comments.body: No. Neither paying to vibe coder or paying to AI artist is getting scammed. You can ask AI to both and get a slop. A person with actual knowledge, on how art or code works, will use AI to get the non slop. Like, artists, will redraw hands and faces to not have wobbly eyes and extra fingers. And you, the inexperienced CEO, will let it slide, and then get surprised "Why my soul prompting called a slop, why no purchases". Well, hypothetically you can be a one man army. A vibe coder, a vibe artists, knowing everything and launching masterpiece project, that doesn't smell like a slop. But as a CEO you would rather pay 2000$ to someone to do a tedious job while taking all the income

comments.author: eliormc
comments.body:
I think the problem now is: if what you want is to pay someone to make your first game because you don't have experience making video games (or the skills), and at the same time you want profit, you are wasting your money, because IT IS your 1st game, and the probability to make a good game the first time is too low!.

I make my first game before AI was a thing, doing everything by myself,  and in my head this was good,  but the reality was: it was my very first game with no experience!, so as you should be thinking, my game failed. So, doesn't matter how intelligent and capable can be the IA or the human programmer, if your game design if bad (because this is your 1st game), then, the programmer or the IA will receive the wrong design and this is destined to fail, and doesn't matter how many tokens you pay or how good the programmer is, if they follow your instructions the game will be garbage when you haven't experience and your way of thinking won't allow you to see what's wrong.
